prompt: Explain to a friend why asking a chatbot the same question twice can give two different answers, and why a fluent answer can still be wrong.

criteria.label: Explains next-token probabilities
criteria.look_for: the model gives possible next words probabilities

criteria.label: Explains sampling
criteria.look_for: the next word is sampled, so likely words usually but not always win, so answers vary

criteria.label: Separates likely from true
criteria.look_for: fluent or likely text is not the same as true, so answers need checking

reference: A chatbot writes one token at a time. For each next token it gives every possible token a probability, then samples one, so the same question can come out differently. Because it picks words that are likely to follow, its writing sounds fluent, but likely is not the same as true, so a fluent answer can still be wrong and needs checking.
